title: improv·artist · naïve (Henri Rousseau)
mutation_directive: improv artist: naïve via Henri Rousseau

improv_extras.practice: untrained jungle paintings; flat foliage, fixed gaze, dreamlike clarity

v1.feedback: The L-system branching structure is legible and the Rousseau palette — deep greens grading to emerald canopy with rare warm flower accents — is well-restrained and true to the brief. The layered depth stacking and flat disc-leaf rendering genuinely channel Rousseau's frontal tableau composition rather than just naming it. To refine: the canopy could be denser at the top so it reads more as an impenetrable wall of foliage (Rousseau leaves no sky gaps); the flat disc particles could benefit from slight size variation by generation so outer leaves feel more like distinct painted shapes rather than uniform confetti; and the entry animation, while charming, is the least Rousseau element — consider starting settled and letting the only motion be the breathing sway.

v2.feedback: The L-system skeleton and canopy-weighted particle distribution are strong structural choices that clearly come from the Rousseau brief — the palette gradient from umber trunk to emerald canopy with rare flower accents is restrained and on-theme. However, additive blending on dark greens will likely merge the dense canopy into a glowing green blob rather than Rousseau's signature flat, distinct, overlapping leaf layers; switch to normal alpha blending or use a leaf-shaped sprite texture to preserve the 'painted' naïveté. The canopy jitter (0.35) may diffuse the L-system branching structure enough that the form reads as a fuzzy mass rather than a recognizable tree silhouette — tighten it to ~0.15 and flatten the disc shapes more aggressively to sell the frontal-tableau layering that defines Rousseau's compositions.
